entries.title: I Corinthians 8:1
segments: Things sacrificed to idols. In very many sacrifices, both among the Jews and the heathen, only a portion was consumed on the altar, the greater part being retained by the worshipper and carried away to be eaten by himself and friends or guests.  The eating of such sacrificial food was deemed an act of worship in honor of the divinity to whom it had been offered (
).  In some cases the feast might be held within the Temple enclosure (
).  It might also be at the worshipper's home or elsewhere.  The sacrificial meat might even be 'sold in the shambles' (
).  For such sacrificial feasts among the Jews, see
.  The eating of such food by a Christian might easily seem, either to heathen or Christian observers, a recognition of idol worship

.
 

 
Knowledge. Intellectual apprehension of truth and duty, which was held by many, especially among the philosophic Greeks, to be all that was required.  The apostle proceeds to show that there is something higher.
 

 
Knowledge puffeth up. Tends to self-confidence and arrogance.
 

 
Love edifieth. As in the margin, 'Buildeth up,' either the individual Christian or the church, as a whole, in Christian character and spiritual grace (

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:2
segments: If any man thinketh that he knoweth anything, etc. He who knows the most sees most clearly how much more there is to know.  In the field of knowledge humility sharpens vision.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:3
segments:
If any man loveth God, etc.  Love brings the soul into touch with God who 'is love,' as no intellectual knowledge can do (1Jn 4.8).
 

 
 Is known by him.  In recognized and approved fellowship and communion (

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:4
segments: That no idol is anything. Instructed Christians did not recognize idols as having any real existence, even as false divinities.  Idols were but empty names.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:7
segments: There is not in all men that knowledge.  Many new converts had not attained this clear conception.  Love will care patiently and tenderly for such.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:9
segments:
Take heed at last, etc. Love cares for the effect of one's example, especially upon those who have less knowledge, or are in any way spiritually 'weak.'
 

 
 A stumblingblock.  An occasion of yielding to temptation or sin.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:10
segments:
Thee who hast knowledge.  An enlightened Christian must make allowance for the narrowness of one who has not his knowledge, and must sometimes therefore deny himself what he sees to be only innocent and beneficial.
 

 
 Sitting at meat in an idol's temple. The strongest case cited as an example.  The weak brother 'sees' the act, but cannot read the motive, which is known only to God.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:13
segments: If meat causeth my brother to stumble, etc.  Rather than risk such a result as mentioned in
, I will make any, even the uttermost, self-denial.  Compare this chapter with
, which discusses the eating of food forbidden by the Jewish ceremonial law, applying to that case the same principles.
